Charged Cartan Monte Carlo — design note v0.1¶

Living design note for the construction that succeeds the “InteractionSimulation” line documented in interaction_history_monte_carlo_writeup.md. v0.1 captures the structural changes agreed during the design discussion that followed the diverging-D_S finding in the Cartan/local-frame model.

Summary of the change vs the prior model¶

The prior model (1-qubit vertices on a Poisson-Delaunay initial layer, Schwinger two-site U for interactions, Cartan/local-frame edge MIs, relaxed eligibility) showed unbounded D_S(σ) growth at all β — diagnosed as a heat-kernel artifact of (a) the ε-floored cross-worldline edges being driven to MI = 0 by separable inputs and (b) the relaxed eligibility creating small-world graphs.

v0.1 keeps the Cartan/local-frame edge structure but adds a discrete charge degree of freedom and the corresponding move set so the frontier is self-regulated by particle/antiparticle dynamics rather than unbounded growth.

Vertices¶

Each vertex v carries:

  • a one-qubit state ρ_v ∈ Eigen::Matrix2cd, evolved as before;

  • a charge q_v ∈ [−1, +1] (real, continuous). Discrete values ±1 and 0 are the special cases used by initial layer / neutral products; pair-creation can produce non-integer charges.

The state and the charge are independent registers — U acts on states, charges are bookkeeping. The charge is a separate quantum number, conserved by U in the same sense the Schwinger fermion-number is a U(1) charge: it commutes with the interaction, and we track it classically.

Interaction unitary U¶

U is a configurable 4×4 two-qubit unitary. Two defaults:

  • Cartan-entangler: a canonical fixed entangler exp(i(c_x XX + c_y YY + c_z ZZ)) with (c_x, c_y, c_z) set by config. Most parsimonious; isolates the entangling content.

  • Schwinger two-site: the current (1/4a)(XX + YY) + (m/2)(−Z⊗I + I⊗Z) Hamiltonian’s exponential — available as a comparator so we don’t lose the Schwinger connection.

The Schwinger construction is no longer load-bearing; v0.1 is honest about being “a discrete graph of MI-coupled qubits with U(1) charge conservation,” not a faithful simulation of the Schwinger model.

Initial layer¶

  • N independent one-qubit random mixed states ρ_v = M M† / Tr(M M†) with M a 2×2 complex Gaussian (no inter-vertex MI; same as current).

  • Charges assigned by mode (cfg.initialChargeMode):

    • ALTERNATING (default): even-index vertices +1, odd-index −1. Exactly Q = 0.

    • RANDOM: each vertex independently ±1 with equal probability. Q ≈ 0 with √N fluctuations.

Delaunay edges are still drawn (for compatibility with the spatial position machinery) but their MI is the ε-floor (separable inputs).

Move set¶

Four moves, replacing the prior interact / un-interact pair:

  1. interact — same-sign bowtie (or with-neutral). Eligibility: pick a random pair (x, y) of frontier vertices with q_x · q_y ≥ 0 (same-sign or at least one neutral). Standard Regge action contribution. Product charges: chargeOf_[U_A] = chargeOf_[A], chargeOf_[V_B] = chargeOf_[B], chargeOf_[Σ_AB] = 0.

  2. unInteract — deep cascade (unchanged from current).

  3. annihilate — partial annihilation, no Regge change. Eligibility: pick a random (+, −) frontier pair (p, m) with q_p > 0, q_m < 0. Rule (charge-only, no vertex deletion — the charges annihilate but the worldlines persist as neutral systems):

    • If q_p + q_m > 0: neutralise m (q_m → 0), update p’s charge to q_p + q_m.

    • If q_p + q_m < 0: neutralise p (q_p → 0), update m’s charge to q_p + q_m < 0.

    • If |q_p + q_m| < ε: both become neutral. Total signed charge Σ q_i is exactly conserved. Total baryon number (count of + minus count of −) can change by ±1 per partial-annihilation event (a vertex’s sign-bucket membership shifts when its charge transitions through zero).

    Why charge-only and not vertex-deletion: a vertex that has been a product of an interaction is referenced from the cell’s vertex list. Deleting it from the spacetime would invalidate the cell. By neutralising the charge but keeping the vertex alive, the geometry stays consistent — only the U(1) quantum number changes. This also matches the QED picture more cleanly: in e⁻e⁺ → γγ the worldlines don’t vanish, the charge content does (the worldlines continue as photon worldlines).

  4. pairCreate — spontaneous pair-creation, no Regge change. Spawn two vertices (p, m) on the frontier with:

    • charges q_p = 0.5 + δ, q_m = −0.5 + δ where δ ∈ [−ε_CP, +ε_CP] is drawn uniformly. ε_CP is the CP-violation bias (config: cfg.cpBias, signed double, default 0).

      • Positive ε_CP favours net + content; negative favours −.

      • At ε_CP = 0 the pair-creation is exactly C/CP-symmetric.

    • joint state: a fixed Bell state |Φ⁺⟩ = (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2 stored in jointOf_[(p, m)]. Bell state is reproducible and maximally entangled.

    • one-qubit marginals on each vertex: Tr_other |Φ⁺⟩⟨Φ⁺| = I/2 (maximally mixed) — S(ρ) = ln 2, populates worldline-self MI.

sweep() proposes the four move types with equal weight by default (configurable); the per-move acceptance handles balance.

Sakharov diagnostic¶

With the partial-annihilation + CP-bias setup, all three Sakharov conditions for baryogenesis are present:

Condition

How it’s met

(i) Baryon-number violation

Partial annihilation can change N_+ − N_− by ±1 per event

(ii) C / CP violation

Non-zero ε_CP biases pair-creation toward + or −

(iii) Out-of-equilibrium

Growth phase (tune()) is far-from-equilibrium; sweep approaches equilibrium

The model can produce a net baryon excess from a Q=0 initial state if ε_CP ≠ 0 and the system departs from equilibrium long enough.

Observables¶

Beyond the existing D_S(σ):

  • getGlobalCharge(): Σ_v q_v over the entire complex. At ε_CP = 0 it’s exactly conserved; at ε_CP ≠ 0 it drifts as a measure of cumulative CP-violation.

  • getChargeProfile(): per-time-slice (N_+, N_−, N_0, Σq | ε_CP > 0). Shows whether charge clusters in time.

  • getChargeCorrelation(maxDist): ⟨q_v · q_w⟩ as a function of graph-distance d(v, w) for d ≤ maxDist. Positive correlation at short distance = same-charge clustering.

  • getModuleCharges(): after a (Louvain / spectral) module decomposition of the MI-weighted graph, the per-module net charge. Reveals matter-dominant vs antimatter-dominant regions. Note: reaching per-module equilibrium will likely take substantial tuning — the dynamics has to keep modules stable long enough for their charge content to settle.

  • getAnnihilationCount() / getPairCreateCount(): cumulative rates of the new moves.

Configurable parameters¶

Numeric parameters (non-experimental):

cfg.beta                 — inverse temperature
cfg.epsilonI             — MI floor for zero edges
cfg.targetInteractions   — T-cap
cfg.cpBias               — CP-violation bias (signed double, default 0)
cfg.initialChargeMode    — ALTERNATING / RANDOM (only if charges enabled)
cfg.unitaryMode          — CARTAN_ENTANGLER / SCHWINGER  (deferred)
cfg.cartanCore           — (c_x, c_y, c_z) for the entangler

Feature flags¶

Experimental features are toggled by boolean flags on InteractionConfig, all named featureXxx (camelCase, matching the rest of the API) and all defaulting to false. New experimental behaviour is always gated behind a flag so old runs are bit-for-bit reproducible. A typical script enables several at once:

cfg = q.InteractionConfig()
cfg.featureCharges                 = True   # v0.1 — charge labels enabled
cfg.featureDeactivateOnAnnihilate  = True   # v0.1.B — annihilation removes from frontier
cfg.featurePhotonOnAnnihilate      = True   # v0.1.iii — spawn photon vertex on annihilation

Each experiment writeup should record the flag configuration it used at the top of the results section.

Current flags:

Flag

Effect

featureCharges

v0.1 charged Cartan: charge labels, annihilate / pairCreate moves, charge observables.

featureDeactivateOnAnnihilate

annihilate removes vertices from the frontier (worldlines terminate) instead of just neutralising their charges. Requires featureCharges.

featurePhotonOnAnnihilate

annihilate also spawns a new neutral “photon” vertex on the frontier, carrying the released information. Requires featureCharges.

featureQuditBasis (deferred to v0.2)

each vertex carries a 4-dim qudit state with charge intrinsic via Q̂. Removes the need for featureCharges (and the v0.1 limitations).

The legacy cfg.useCharges flag is preserved as an alias for cfg.featureCharges — setting either enables the charged-Cartan code paths. Dependent flags are auto-cleared when featureCharges is off, so a partially-configured run can’t enter an undefined state.

What v0.1 does NOT include (deferred to v0.2+)¶

  • 4-dim qudit basis — see “v0.2 sketch” below.

  • Explicit photon vertex on annihilation events to restore energy bookkeeping (currently energy is non-conserved by the partial- annihilation move).

  • Cosmological constant Λ_0 as an independent parameter — frontier self-regulation via annihilation removes the need for it in v0.1, but having it back as a tuning dial could expose a wider phase diagram.

  • Face-glue moves — discussed and held in reserve. May become unnecessary if charge clustering provides the inter-cell coupling we were after.

  • Tunable Cartan core scan as an experiment — scan (c_x, c_y, c_z) to find which entangling structures support 4D emergence.

Implementation order (v0.1)¶

  1. Add chargeOf_, cfg.useCharges, cfg.cpBias, cfg.initialChargeMode.

  2. Add cfg.unitaryMode and the Cartan-entangler U builder.

  3. Modify interact eligibility (same-sign / with-neutral).

  4. Modify product-charge inheritance in interact accept.

  5. Implement annihilate and pairCreate.

  6. Plumb the four observables.

  7. Smoke test, β-scan, charge-correlation analysis.

Initial v0.1 β-scan results (cpBias = 0)¶

Same scan parameters as the chargeless-v2 scatter for direct comparison: N=8, T=3000, 22 β log-spaced in [10⁻⁴, 5×10⁻³], 10 seeds per β, K=15, σ-grid extended to 10¹⁰.

Per-β mean ± std peak D_S, with σ-saturation count in parentheses:

        β    |    v0.1 (charges on)       |    v2 (chargeless)
   1.0e-4   |  198.19 ± 103.49 (0/10)    |    0.07 ±  0.01 (0/10)
   3.06e-4  |  280.21 ± 100.81 (0/10)    |    0.38 ±  0.36 (0/10)
   1.00e-3  |     ~245    (range)        |    0.96 ±  0.15 (5/10)
   1.635e-3 |  216.07 ±  98.32 (0/10)    |    3.73 ±  0.54 (10/10)
   3.45e-3  |  272.76 ± 113.11 (0/10)    |   10.80 ±  1.85 (10/10)
   5.00e-3  |  250.75 ±  79.05 (0/10)    |   10.22 ±  2.27 (10/10)

Three findings:

  1. All phase structure collapses. The v2 scan had clean zero-D / extended-D / high-D phases at different β. v0.1 has a single flat regime: peak D_S ≈ 250 ± 100 at every β value. The charge dynamics (annihilate / pairCreate) equilibrate so quickly that they wash out the action’s ability to select different geometries.

  2. No σ-saturation anywhere. Where v2 had all-saturated readings at high β (D_S(σ) still rising at σ = 10⁶), v0.1’s D_S(σ) curves turn over inside the σ ≤ 10¹⁰ grid at all β. The peak measure is meaningful again.

  3. Charge conservation is exact (Q_global = 0 at every record) and ±vertex-count balance holds to ~±10% per seed even though individual vertex charges drift. So the bookkeeping is sound.

Interpretation. We’ve traded one pathology (v2’s runaway-D_S + σ-saturation) for a different non-physical regime (homogeneous small-world graphs at all β). Neither produces a clean D_S = 4 plateau. The charge dynamics are too aggressive — every interact proposal has to compete with annihilate and pairCreate, which fire ~3× more often combined and don’t carry any β-dependence in their acceptance.

Known v0.1 limitations¶

Q drift under un-interact after annihilation¶

The frontier-summed Q_global is exactly conserved under the forward-only moves (interact, annihilate, pairCreate) at cpBias = 0. It is not conserved under unInteract when there have been intervening annihilations.

The reason is a tension between the classical-label representation of charge in v0.1 and the historical semantics of un-interact:

  • When interact(x, y) runs, the worldline products U_A, V_B inherit their parent’s charge, chargeOf_[U_A] = chargeOf_[x].

  • An annihilate(U_A, m) event can later change chargeOf_[U_A] without changing chargeOf_[x] (the parent on the past slice still has its original charge).

  • When unInteract later removes the cell that created U_A, it restores x to the frontier with its still-original charge. But U_A’s charge (and m’s, if it survived) is now different from what it was at consumption time.

Net effect: Q_frontier after the un-interact can differ from Q_frontier before, by the amount the annihilation neutralised.

feature_deactivate_on_annihilate does NOT eliminate this drift. Deactivation cleanly removes the annihilated vertices from the frontier, but the drift comes from un-interact restoring a parent of one side of an annihilation event (e.g., x, the producer of xp) while the partner side (m, paired with xp in the annihilation) isn’t accounted for — m was produced by a different cell that’s not being un-interacted. The conservation requires un-interact to cascade through annihilation events to the partner’s history, which isn’t implemented.

The covered regression tests testUnInteractCanDriftQWithAnnihilation and testDeactivateOnAnnihilateDocumentedDrift pin this behaviour explicitly so it’s stable until v0.2 changes it intentionally.

To eliminate the drift would require either:

  • annihilation events become first-class objects in the un-interact cascade BFS (treat annihilation as a “fake cell” linking the two worldline-producing cells); or

  • v0.2’s qudit basis, where charge is intrinsic to the state and any modification (including annihilation) is propagated unitarily along the worldline.

Next round of experiments¶

To diagnose / address:

  1. CP-bias scan. Vary cfg.cpBias at a few fixed β to see whether asymmetric pair-creation produces spatial clustering of charge (the inhomogeneous-baryogenesis hypothesis). Specifically:

    • Does Q_global drift saturate or grow unbounded?

    • Does the charge profile show domain-wall-like structure?

    • Does peak D_S depend on cpBias?

  2. Weighted-move sweep. Change the sweep weights from uniform-1/4 to favour interact (e.g., 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.15 / 0.15 for interact / unInteract / annihilate / pairCreate). Restore the action’s selective power. Expected: phase structure re-emerges; D_S becomes β-dependent again.

  3. Cluster-purity observable. Implement getModuleCharges and the purity-ranked version (getModulePurityProfile) described in the v0.2 sketch. Run on existing v0.1 records to see if even at Q = 0 globally there are pure ±clusters spatially separated. This is the actual baryogenesis test.

  4. v0.2 implementation. Promote vertices to ququarts with charge encoded intrinsically via the Q̂ operator. Re-run the scan to test whether quantum charge superpositions behave differently from classical-label charges.

The CP-bias scan and the cluster-purity observable are the most diagnostic; the weighted-move sweep is the easiest fix; v0.2 is the biggest implementation lift but the most principled.

v0.2 sketch: 4-dim qudit vertices (Dirac-spinor style)¶

Vertices are no longer one-qubit but one-ququart (one qudit of dim 4) with basis

{ |+, 0⟩, |+, 1⟩, |−, 0⟩, |−, 1⟩ }

The first label is the charge sector (matter / antimatter, the particle-vs-antiparticle register); the second is the spin / occupation (the existing qubit content). This is exactly the component structure of a Dirac spinor at a spacetime point.

What changes¶

  • State storage per vertex becomes Eigen::Matrix4cd.

  • Charge becomes intrinsic: the operator Q̂ = diag(+1, +1, −1, −1) acts on the 4-dim register; ⟨q⟩_v = Tr[ρ_v Q̂] ∈ [−1, +1] is read out from the state.

  • The classical chargeOf_ label is removed. The continuous-charge feature of v0.1 emerges automatically from mixed-state 4-dim ρ.

  • Quantum charge superpositions are now possible — a vertex can be in (|+,0⟩ + |−,1⟩)/√2, with ⟨q⟩ = 0 but not a classical mixture of + and −. The dynamics can then exhibit charge-interference effects.

  • C and CP are operators, not parameters. Charge conjugation Ĉ = X_charge ⊗ I_spin (swap the charge register). CP-violation becomes “U doesn’t commute with Ĉ ⊗ P̂ on the bipartite Hilbert space” — a clean operator statement.

  • Annihilation becomes a quantum amplitude: project the joint state onto the charge-singlet subspace, weighted by amplitude.

  • U is now 16×16 acting on two qudits.

Cost¶

  • Per-vertex state: 4× larger (16 complex numbers vs 4).

  • Per-joint state: 16× larger (256 complex numbers vs 16).

  • Partial-trace / MI / matrix-multiply ops scale roughly as the dimension cubed → ~50–100× slower per interaction event.

  • Implementation effort: a substantial refactor of computeInteraction, partialTrace, traceOutFirst/Second, tensor2, jointMutualInformation, plus all consumers. The bowtie topology and Regge machinery are unchanged.

Decomposition of the 16×16 U¶

For SU(4) we had the magic-basis Cartan / KAK decomposition

U = (K₁ ⊗ K₂) · exp(i (c_x XX + c_y YY + c_z ZZ)) · (K₃ ⊗ K₄)

cleanly splitting “local frames” from “entangling core”. There is no equally clean canonical decomposition for SU(16). Options, in order of usefulness:

  • Operator Schmidt decomposition (recommended). Any operator U: H_A ⊗ H_B → H_A ⊗ H_B on a bipartite Hilbert space has a Schmidt decomposition

    U = Σ_k σ_k (A_k ⊗ B_k)

    with {A_k} and {B_k} orthonormal operator bases on each side (under the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product ⟨X, Y⟩ = Tr(X†Y)) and σ_k ≥ 0. The operator Schmidt rank (count of non-zero σ_k) is 1 iff U = A ⊗ B is purely local. Rank > 1 measures genuine entangling content; the σ-spectrum quantifies how much. Computationally: reshape U_{ij,kl} (with i,k indexing H_A and j,l indexing H_B) into a d_A² × d_B² matrix and SVD it — the singular values are the σ_k. This is the natural generalisation of the Cartan core (c_x, c_y, c_z) to higher dimensions. It loses the discrete “local left + local right” rotation labelling but preserves the “local content vs entangling content” split that we actually use.

  • Khaneja–Glaser recursive Cartan. Recursively applies KAK to nested subspaces of SU(2^n). For two ququarts (n=4 qubits) it gives a depth-O(n) decomposition into local + Cartan-core layers, with many parameters but a definite tree structure. Useful if we ever need to generate a Haar-random U with explicit local/entangling structure.

  • Quantum Shannon decomposition. Compiles any unitary into a sequence of single-qubit rotations and CNOTs (or any universal gate set). Standard in quantum circuit compilation. Doesn’t give a “local + entangling core” split — gives a circuit.

  • Naked SVD on U as a 16×16 matrix. U = X · Σ · Y† with Σ = I (since U is unitary, all singular values are 1). Loses everything we care about — it’s a trivial reformulation. SVD only becomes useful when applied to the operator-Schmidt reshape above.

Σ_AB as Choi state of U¶

The Choi–Jamiolkowski isomorphism gives us a principled state to put on the entangling-core vertex Σ_AB, rather than the ad-hoc proxy used in v0.1. For a 4-dim × 4-dim unitary U, the Choi state J(U) = (U ⊗ I)|Ω⟩⟨Ω|(U† ⊗ I) is a pure state on a 256-dim doubled Hilbert space, and its bipartite Schmidt decomposition has exactly the same coefficients as the operator Schmidt decomposition of U. The Choi state literally is the canonical “entangling content of U” as a quantum state — the proper generalisation of the SU(4) Cartan core.

This raises the dimension-mismatch question: Σ_AB carries up to a 256-dim state while worldline vertices (U_A, V_B and ordinary ququarts) carry 4-dim states. How does the heterogeneous interaction work?

Three coherent options:

(A) Reduce-before-interaction (v0.2 default). When a 4-dim worldline vertex interacts with a higher-dim Σ-vertex, project the Σ-state onto a measurement basis matching the worldline’s structure (e.g., its charge-eigenbasis), giving a 4-dim collapsed state. Then apply the standard 16×16 U. The Σ_AB vertex’s full Choi state is used at the moment of bowtie creation for principled per-edge MI calculations, but is collapsed to 4-dim on subsequent interaction. Physical analog: Compton scattering / decoherence at the interaction vertex. The worldline acts as a measurement device on the photon-like Σ; only the part of Σ aligned with the worldline’s structure participates.

(B) Promote-to-higher-dim (deferred — too expensive at our scale). Lift the 4-dim worldline state to the 256-dim space via ρ_4 ⊗ (I_64 / 64), then apply a 65536×65536 U on the full joint and extract marginals. Preserves all Choi content, but costs scale by ~10⁴×. Honest but probably untenable for research-scale runs.

(C) Inert Σ_AB (deferred — drops a dynamics channel). Σ_AB carries full Choi at creation and is never eligible for further interactions. It participates in the spectral-graph topology and contributes to per-edge MIs forever, but does not get consumed as an input to a future interact. Physical analog: virtual photon / ephemeral mediator. Loses Σ-Σ scattering (the photon-photon analog).

(A) is the v0.2 default. (B) and (C) are kept as variants worth playing with — (B) gives the gold-standard treatment if compute is cheap enough, (C) gives the cleanest “interaction-quantum-as-frozen- record” reading.

Cluster-homogeneity-ranked charge observable¶

The v0.1 getModuleCharges observable returns net charge per community-detected module of the MI-weighted graph. For testing the inhomogeneous-baryogenesis hypothesis we need a sharper view: rank clusters by their charge homogeneity / purity and read off the CP-violation signature from the most-pure modules.

Concretely:

  • For each detected module M, compute the charge purity

    P(M) = |Σ_{v ∈ M} q_v| / Σ_{v ∈ M} |q_v|

    bounded in [0, 1]: P = 0 means perfectly balanced, P = 1 means every charged vertex has the same sign. This is the natural “matter-dominance ratio” of a region.

  • Sort modules by P descending. The top-k modules are the “most-pure” matter- or antimatter-dominated regions.

  • Report:

    • The fraction of total volume in high-purity modules (the “domain-wall fraction”).

    • The mean signed charge of the top-k modules (does the matter-dominance bias replicate at the cluster level even when global Q ≈ 0?).

    • The size distribution of charge-pure modules (does the geometry select a few large pure clusters, or many small ones?).

If the dynamics genuinely produces inhomogeneous baryogenesis from near-zero ε_CP, we’d expect to see a small number of large high-purity modules — i.e., the universe naturally separates into matter-dominated and antimatter-dominated regions even with C/CP near-symmetry. Reproducing the observed-universe asymmetry would mean identifying one such pure cluster and treating its perspective as the “observable universe”.

This generalises straightforwardly to v0.2’s continuous charges (charges in [-1, +1] from the qudit-state read-out via Q̂) — the purity formula |Σ q| / Σ |q| is well-defined for any charge values.

Practical plan for v0.2¶

We don’t need a fully general U-parameterisation for the experiment. The pragmatic path is:

  1. Pick a fixed canonical 16×16 U built from a parameterised Hamiltonian on the bipartite ququart system, e.g., a “Dirac-pair Hamiltonian”:

    H = J · (Q̂_A · Q̂_B)        ← charge-charge coupling
    + α · (σ_A · σ_B)         ← spin-spin coupling
    + β · (Ĉ_A ⊗ Ĉ_B + h.c.)  ← charge-conjugation coupling

    with J, α, β configurable. Exponentiate to get U = exp(−i H δt).

  2. Compute the operator Schmidt decomposition of U once at construction time; report the σ-spectrum as a diagnostic (how entangling is this U?).

  3. Compute and store J(U) once at construction time — pure 256-dim state encoding U’s full entangling content.

  4. Apply U as a black-box 16×16 multiply on 4-dim × 4-dim joint states during ordinary worldline-worldline interactions.

  5. For Σ_AB-worldline interactions: project Σ_AB’s state onto its charge-eigenbasis (4-dim collapse), then apply U as above.

  6. Read out charge expectation values from each vertex’s ρ_v via Tr[ρ_v Q̂] whenever the move set needs charges (eligibility, annihilation matching, pair-creation distribution).

This sidesteps the SU(16) decomposition problem entirely — we use a chosen U, not a decomposed arbitrary U. The Cartan core’s analog (the entangling content) is read out via the operator Schmidt decomposition / Choi state as a one-time diagnostic at construction.

Implementation order (v0.2)¶

  1. Promote SystemState from Matrix2cd to Matrix4cd.

  2. Generalise partialTrace, traceOutFirst/Second, tensor2, jointMutualInformation to d=4.

  3. Define Q̂, Ĉ, and the ququart Pauli analogs as constants.

  4. Build a parameterised Dirac-pair Hamiltonian and its 16×16 U.

  5. Re-port interact, annihilate, pairCreate to read charges from states (no chargeOf_ map).

  6. Operator-Schmidt diagnostic on U at construction time.

  7. Smoke test, then re-run v0.1’s experiment suite at v0.2 vertex dimensionality for comparison.
